title: 1 IN 2
description: World Premiere | Gala Screening Please note: All proceeds from this screening will be donated by the filmmaker to Maggie's. After being diagnosed with stage 4 bowel cancer, filmmaker David Nicholas Wilkinson set out to investigate a disease that is increasingly affecting younger people and to understand why its symptoms are so often overlooked. Featuring patients, doctors and cancer specialists, 1 IN 2 challenges common misconceptions, explores the realities of modern cancer treatment and asks whether we really know the signs to look out for. Honest, eye-opening and unexpectedly funny, this is a powerful film that aims to dispel myths, raise awareness and, above all, offer hope. Because knowing the signs could save your life.

title: Doc | Dinner | Drink: Arcadia
description: As part of this event, Central Scotland Documentary Festival is delighted to present the 2026 Stirling 900 Award for Achievement in Documentary to John Archer, recognising his outstanding contribution to documentary film and Scotland’s screen culture. Founder and Managing Director of Hopscotch Films, John has produced an exceptional body of work including The Story of Film: An Odyssey, Arcadia, My Old School, Tish and I Am Belfast. A former Head of Music and Arts at BBC Scotland and founding Chief Executive of Scottish Screen, his influence extends far beyond his work as a producer. We are thrilled to welcome John to Stirling and celebrate a career defined by collaboration and an enduring commitment to documentary storytelling. Directed by BAFTA-winning director Paul Wright, Arcadia explores Britain’s changing relationship with its land. Moving from village celebrations and seasonal rituals to farming, industry and lost crafts, the film reveals a landscape shaped by tradition, transformation and time. A vivid and often unsettling portrait of rural Britain, Arcadia captures the beauty, brutality, magic and madness of our relationship with the land, and with one another. Using over 100 years of archive footage, Arcadia is accompanied with a grand, expressive new score by Adrian Utley of Portishead and Will Gregory of Goldfrapp. Every ticket includes admission to the documentary, a main course (vegan/gluten free) and an alcoholic or soft drink. description: Central Scotland Documentary Festival is thrilled to welcome filmmaker Finlay Pretsell to Stirling to open this year’s festival with Douglas Gordon by Douglas Gordon - a compelling portrait of one of Scotland’s most celebrated contemporary artists. Douglas Gordon by Douglas Gordon is an unflinchingly raw and intimate portrait of the celebrated boundary pushing artist which blurs the border between reality and performance. Raised in Glasgow, Scotland during the Margaret Thatcher era, Gordon is among the most important and influential artists of his generation. Best known for his films and large-scale video installations such as “24 Hour Psycho” and the 2006 Cannes masterpiece “Zidane: A 21st Century Portrait”. Gordon reveals his soul and innermost thoughts whilst making new work and reflecting on his advancing years through spontaneous acts and conversation. As the filmmaker-subject relationship shifts from collaborative intimacy to a more complex dynamic we wonder, who is actually making this film? Through this multifaceted portrait, we witness how Gordon has sacrificed everything for his art. Q&A Following the screening there will be a Q&A with director Finlay Pretsell. title: Eastern European Surrealism - Manipulate Arts Autumn Animation Season
description: This shorts programme is curated in partnership with Samizdat Eastern European Film Festival in Glasgow and offers a unique collection of Eastern European surrealist animation from 1965 to 2022. This retrospective offers a whistlestop tour through the rich history of animation from Eastern Europe and Central Asia, and exploring the ways in which this history is still influencing animators in the region today. From a city run by beans to an office building filled with anti‑capitalist mice, these films represent not just the technical finesse and playfulness of animation, but also the intricate ways in which it captures the political and social anxieties of this geographic region. The showcase represents a fantastic opportunity for audiences in Stirling to see rarely exhibited films that have defined animation from the middle of the twentieth century to the present day. Manipulate Arts’ Autumn Animation Season is supported by Film Hub Scotland, part of the BFI’s Film Audience Network, awarding funding on behalf of Screen Scotland and the BFI National Lottery

title: OTOXO Universities Workshop
description:
For 2026, Central Scotland Documentary Festival is offering a unique workshop for all emerging or aspiring filmmakers currently at university, providing them with the key insights they need to produce their first professional documentaries and survive in the industry. The workshop will be hosted by OTOXO Productions. OTOXO Productions is an award-winning documentary production company based in Barcelona, making films for Amazon Prime, Apple TV, Filmin, The Guardian and TV3, while winning selections and prizes at some of the world’s top documentary festivals, including DocsBarcelona, FIPADOC, REFRAME, MakeDox and, of course, CSDF. They create character-focused documentaries for cinema, TV, festival and online audiences, and are ideally placed to host this workshop because, in parallel with their productions, they run The INto INdustry Programme - one-month and one-year programmes combining rigorous training and professional experience, which specialise in giving young people the creative, technical and professional skills they need to become directors and industry professionals. The workshop will include a combination of presentation, viewing, discussion and group activities, focusing on crucial aspects of the industry such as:

  • Finding inspiring characters and constructing great narratives
  • Directing in a real-life documentary environment
  • The key skills behind shooting broadcast-standard visual material
  • Getting through the edit
  • Building contacts and collaborating
  • Surviving financially as an independent filmmaker
And, if you have any ideas that you’d like to develop for your own film, OTOXO would love to hear about them too, so that you can get some professional workshopping to push your own documentary visions forward. Just drop a couple of lines (or more if you like!) to John@otoxoproductions.com before the event, or share it on the day! This will be an inspiring and insightful event for anyone who hopes to make their own industry-standard documentaries.

title: The Last First: K2
description: In "The Last First: Winter K2," Amir Bar-Lev tells a complex, harrowing, and moving story that takes an unflinching look at the industry of extreme mountain climbing and its changing culture. Focusing on a 2021 expedition, this documentary follows Icelander John Snorri Sigurjónsson and the Pakistani father-son team of Ali and Sajid Sadpara, a party of mountaineers who set out to be the first to summit K2 in the winter, when the mountain’s conditions are the cruelest. The men soon find themselves sharing the treacherous ascent with influencer climbers and their film crews, commercial expedition clients, and a Nepalese team no longer content to help Westerners achieve mountaineering glory. "The Last First: Winter K2" takes us to the icy heights and unpredictable weather of K2 and reveals a surprising and layered story—one of strategy and determination, class and caste, money and power—all under life-and-death circumstances.

She’s swept off her feet by the charming Knave of Hearts, who’s on the run for stealing the tarts. Confusion piles upon confusion. Then Alice wakes with a start. Was it all a daydream? Christopher Wheeldon’s Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland burst onto the stage in 2011 in an explosion of colour, stage magic and inventive, sophisticated choreography. Bob Crowley’s wildly imaginative, eye-popping designs draw on everything from puppetry to projections to make Wonderland wonderfully real. The result shows The Royal Ballet at its best, bringing together world-class dance with enchanting family entertainment and ingenious music and design.

title: The Royal Ballet - Manon

A native of this hedonistic underworld, Manon is caught between twin desires when she falls in love with the student Des Grieux. Steadfast and devoted, he offers the possibility of an honourable life. Yet, the riches promised by the world of Parisian society remain tempting... description: At a cosy Christmas party, young Clara meets the mysterious magician Drosselmeyer, who gives her a nutcracker doll. When the guests have departed and the house is asleep, Clara sneaks downstairs in search of the doll. Instead, she finds Drosselmeyer, who whisks her away on a journey into a whole world of enchantment: fantastical landscapes of flurried snow and glittering confection where toys come alive and the magic never stops. Peter Wright’s production of this festive family favourite sparkles to the wondrous swell of Tchaikovsky’s orchestral score, alongside the glow and grandeur of Julia Trevelyan Oman’s period designs.

title: The Royal Opera - Carmen
description: Under the oppressive heat of the Spanish sun, the fiercely independent Carmen attracts the attention of Don José. She warns him not to fall in love with her, but his obsession knows no bounds. Damiano Michieletto’s searing production returns, casting scorching light on the lust, violence and destructive desire of Bizet’s ever-popular opera. An all-star cast brings this white-hot drama to life, with Ginger Costa-Jackson in the fiery title role, alongside Russell Thomas as the jealous and despairing Don José. Following his 2023 Royal Opera debut, Sesto Quatrini returns to conduct Bizet’s electrifying and sensual score.

title: The Royal Opera - Così fan tutte
description: Spurred on by a bet, two young men hatch a plan to test the fidelity of their girlfriends. What follows is a slippery game of seduction and power, the four lovers plunging into a dizzying world of shifting reality, where truth becomes increasingly unstable. Così fan tutte has lost none of its sting since it first scandalised audiences in 1790. In her Main Stage debut, Netia Jones, Associate Director of The Royal Opera, reimagines Mozart’s comedy of manners through a sharp contemporary lens, where 18th-century romantic trickery meets deeply satirical high-tech deceit. Taking on the roles of the lovers is an exciting young cast led by Louise Alder, Simone McIntosh, Mingjie Lei and Huw Montague Rendall, with Gerald Finley as their manipulative game-master Don Alfonso and Emily Pogorelc as Despina. Thomas Hengelbrock conducts, bringing out the exquisite melodies that underpin the provocative, and resolutely modern, themes at the heart of the opera.

title: The Royal Opera - Götterdämmerung
description: An earth in ruin. The twilight of the Gods. Deception leads to treachery, then devastation, when Siegfried is tricked into betraying Brünnhilde. Learning the truth of her beloved’s innocence, Brünnhilde at last returns the ring to the Rhinemaidens, before ordering that Valhalla be swallowed in flames. For the long-awaited finale of Wagner’s epic saga, director Barrie Kosky situates the rich apocalyptic drama in a contemporary world of dream-like turmoil. Antonio Pappano, Conductor Laureate of The Royal Opera, returns to take on the impassioned, otherworldly music – including Siegfried’s transporting Funeral March and Brünnhilde’s electrifying Immolation Scene. The brilliant cast is led by Elisabet Strid, Andreas Schager and Mika Kares, who together with the full forces of the Orchestra of the Royal Opera House and the Royal Opera Chorus bring opera’s greatest journey to its shattering end.

title: The Short Film Award
description:
Discover fresh talent and powerful storytelling in this year’s short film strand. 11 films will be screened, each in the running for the inaugural Short Film Award, chosen by audience vote.

5th SPRING

A SIN DE FELLA STORY

Sheryn Yidi | UK 2026 | 15 mins Sin de Fella and her chosen family of performers prepare a new cabaret show, but behind the spectacle lies the constant pressure of keeping their creative home alive.

BERMUDA RIOTS ARE DIFFERENT

Alyson Thompson, Matt Mead | UK 2026 | 6 mins A look back at Bermuda’s troubled history of racial unrest between 1968 and 1977, alongside a triangle of colonial influences: Bermuda, Great Britain and the USA.

CAPTAIN JACK, THE PIRATE CAT OF HATTER'S HALL

Tom Parsons | UK 2026 | 7 mins He’s a sassy old cat who sits in the sun outside a second-hand record shop, but it might surprise you to find out about his past, and about just how special he is to the people who come and visit him.

EARTHBEAT

Noora Lappalainen | Finland, UK 2026 | 10 mins Nature recordist’s microphone becomes a lifeline to the wild, capturing echoes of a world that is struggling to be heard.

EMRAA MIN WARD

Al Ameel Abdul Azeez | United Arab Emirates 2026 | 13 mins In Oman’s Jabal Akhdar mountains, a young widow defies tradition to become the region’s first female rose farmer, forging an independent life against the odds.

HOME

Audrey Grant | UK 2026 | 6 mins A personal reflection on the loss of place through the lens of visual artist, Audrey Grant after returning to Grangemouth.

title: The Story of Documentary Film - Part One
description: The Central Scotland Documentary Festival is delighted to present the 2026 Stirling 900 Award for Achievement in Documentary to John Archer, recognising his outstanding contribution to documentary film and Scotland’s screen culture. John Archer has a longstanding creative relationship with Mark Cousins, having produced many of his films. As part of our celebration of John as this year’s recipient of the Stirling 900 Award for Achievement in Documentary, we are delighted to present Part One of The Story of Documentary Film. Part one of this exploration of documentary takes us back to where it all began, exploring the pioneering years of 1895 to 1918. Visiting the very buildings where some of the earliest films were made, Cousins uncovers how imagination, innovation and passion shaped the emerging art form. title: We, the Hated
description: Scottish Premiere Central Scotland Documentary Festival is proud to bring this year’s festival to a close with We, the Hated, Rich Felgate’s urgent and unflinching documentary exploring the people and forces shaping Britain’s increasingly divided political landscape. A filmmaker gets more than he bargained for when his girlfriend is part of starting one of the most polarising protest movements in recent memory: Just Stop Oil. We, The Hated tells the inside story of how a group of every-day concerned citizens hatch a contentious plan of civil disobedience to wake the country up to the climate emergency. And what the government does to shut them down. As irreversible climate tipping points loom and their controversial protests face mounting repression, four activists - Indigo, Mark, Phoebe, and Jane - must weigh the personal cost of action against the existential stakes of inaction.
